interpretation: Occupancy and provenance evidence are strongly complementary: each identifies histories the other cannot.
Adding provenance to the complete v22 occupancy library increased exact history identification from 579 to 687 of 768 design rows.
Provenance-only evidence rescued 90 of the 189 v22 occupancy-unresolved design rows, and the combined library rescued 108.
Static unique-origin provenance tags never separated activation histories; history-sensitive provenance information arose only where multiple source basins could contribute.
Even the complete occupancy plus provenance libraries left 81 design rows unresolved for exact activation history.
The equilibrium-provenance target was never harder than exact history and yielded many strict target-specific measurement savings.
claim_boundary: Provenance tags are idealized earliest-source observations, not empirical ancestry or admixture.
Equal unit measurement count is combinatorial burden rather than field cost.
The 81 unresolved rows establish non-identifiability only for the frozen three histories and observation libraries.
The next question should test whether the residual exact-history aliases differ on any declared ecological consequence before seeking a new observation type.
